transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-04-14 07:32 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees (Redwood): Alex Chen (AE), Priya Mehta (SE), Jordan Park (CSM)
Attendees (Atlas Commerce): Daniel Ortiz - Head of Procurement, Leah Kim - Legal, Ibrahim Nadeem - Security Lead, Maya Torres - VP Eng, Samir Patel - FinOps

Summary:
Quick alignment on procurement readiness, outstanding SLA items, pricing clarity for committed capacity vs burst, and privacy/KMS expectations for a Private deployment pilot. Agreed to share redlined SLA, benchmark plan and security artifact list.

Topics:
- MSA/DPA redlines and fee schedule
- SLA SLOs for 99th percentile latency and uptime credits
- Dedicated vs hosted cost tradeoffs and reserved commit levels
- KMS, encryption at rest, and audit artifact requests
- Pilot success criteria and timeline

Transcript:
[00:00] Alex Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick roll call. I'll kick off — we want to make sure the procurement path and privacy asks are captured.
[00:18] Daniel Ortiz: Thanks, Alex. Atlas is under a finance review so need final pricing and clear SLA before we move to exec sign-off.
[00:28] Alex Chen: Understood. For context I'm Alex, AE, and Priya's our SE. Priya, can you do a quick intro to the deployment options?
[00:36] Priya Mehta: Yeah hi, Priya here. So Redwood has three deployment flavors: hosted API, dedicated capacity — that's reserved GPU pools — and private, which can be a VPC or on-prem depending on needs. For pilot we recommend Redwood Dedicated in their VPC peering mode so you get isolation plus predictable throughput.
[00:56] Maya Torres: For us isolation and audit logs are non-negotiable. We can't send PII to a shared tenant. We need either VPC or on-prem and explicit KMS support.
[01:10] Priya Mehta: Totally — KMS integrations are supported, we can do customer-managed keys for the private control plane. Note there are some differences in key management between on-prem and cloud VPC options.
[01:26] Ibrahim Nadeem: Quick question — do you support HSM-backed keys or only cloud KMS? Our compliance team requires HSM or HSM-backed KMS for certain data classes.
[01:38] Alex Chen: We have HSM integrations via partners and can bring a path for enterprise customers — not out of the box for all plans but available under Private deploy with enterprise license. We'll include details.
[01:50] Leah Kim: On the MSA/DPA: our privacy team flagged data retention language and subprocessors. We need a list of subprocessors for the Private offering even if it's a customer-managed VPC. Also, indemnity caps and data destruction at termination need explicit language.
[02:08] Alex Chen: We'll send the subprocessors list. For termination data destruction, we can propose a 30-day purge window and certification. I'll put that in the redline.
[02:18] Samir Patel: Pricing — we want clarity on committed reserved capacity vs burst pricing. Also need an hourly burn model for spikes.
[02:29] Priya Mehta: Pricing model: baseline reserved instance monthly commit + burstable capacity at defined per-token tiers. We can provide a pricing worksheet with examples that map to your token distributions. There will be discounts for longer-term commits.
[02:44] Daniel Ortiz: Any penalties or credits tied to SLA? Our procurement team needs to see measurable service credits for missing latency or availability targets.
[02:53] Alex Chen: We typically define uptime SLO and a 99th percentile latency SLO for requests under N tokens. Credits scale with length of outage or missed P99. We can propose specific tiers. Priya, want to weigh in on latency SLOs for our Dedicated environment?
[03:06] Priya Mehta: On Dedicated we can guarantee throughput and baseline P95/P99 under a provided traffic pattern. Important caveat: tails can vary with huge context lengths; we recommend sample prompt sets for benchmarking. For a typical 512-token distribution, P99 targets of ~350-450ms are realistic on modern GPUs; but that depends on model family and quantization.
[03:30] Maya Torres: That number is helpful. We will run a perf test. We need a test plan and a runbook beforehand.
[03:37] Priya Mehta: We'll share a perf test script and a runbook for KV cache priming and warmup. Also notes on batch-size controls and tokenization differences.
[03:49] Leah Kim: About the DPA — we're also blocking on data residency. Atlas has EU customer data; we want confirmation the private control plane can be in eu-west and logs be retained in EU or purged.
[04:01] Alex Chen: Yes, regional control planes and log residency are supported for Private deployments. We'll include the region mapping for your account.
[04:09] Ibrahim Nadeem: Audit artifacts — what can Redwood provide for SOC2? Full Type II or just a summary? We need access to control narratives and a copy of the report if possible.
[04:20] Jordan Park: Jordan here — we can provide SOC2 Type II summary and a PDF redacted version for procurement. For deeper requests, we can run an on-site or secure review under NDA.
[04:32] Ibrahim Nadeem: Okay, that's fine. Also need details on key rotation and compartmentalization of logs.
[04:39] Priya Mehta: Key rotation for customer-managed KMS follows your KMS provider, we recommend rotation policies and supporting HSM-based keys in Private. Logs can be shipped to your SIEM via syslog/S3 with retention policies you control in the VPC peer path.
[04:58] Daniel Ortiz: On the contract side — payment terms and termination clauses. We prefer net-45, but can do net-30 if there's a committed multi-month contract. Late fees aside, any flexibility?
[05:10] Alex Chen: Commercially we can be flexible. For enterprise agreements we usually negotiate payment terms in the commercial schedule. We'll flag finance for tradeoffs on net terms vs pricing.
[05:21] Samir Patel: Need to understand what happens if Atlas exceeds committed throughput — is throttling automatic or do we get billed at burst rates?
[05:30] Priya Mehta: Overflow behavior is policy-driven. Options: throttle, fallback to a smaller model variant, or allow burst billing. We'll let you pick the policy and test.
[05:40] Maya Torres: Fallback to a smaller model is risky if output quality matters; we prefer controlled burst billing and an alerting window.
[05:47] Priya Mehta: That's common, you can set thresholds and alerts before automatic fallback.
[05:54] Leah Kim: For DPA - subprocessors, does Redwood use cloud providers for storage? We need a list and their data center locations.
[06:03] Alex Chen: Yes, we'll share the subprocessors list and regional mapping. For Private, the footprint is minimized but there are still infra partners.
[06:10] Ibrahim Nadeem: Encryption at rest — can we bring our own key into the RW-managed control plane?
[06:15] Priya Mehta: Customer-managed keys are supported for the private control plane. On-prem gives you full control; VPC peering supports BYOK via your cloud KMS projects.
[06:25] Daniel Ortiz: Let's talk timeline. We're targeting a pilot with limited tenant by end of May. Legal needs the SLA and DPA redlines two weeks before exec sign-off.
[06:35] Alex Chen: So we'll aim to deliver redlined SLA and pricing worksheet by 2026-04-16. Perf test plan and runbook by 2026-04-18. Does that work for you?
[06:44] Maya Torres: Yes that timeline is tight but doable. We'll prioritize.
[06:48] Samir Patel: On pricing, please include an example bill for our monthly baseline with a 20% monthly spike. We need to model FinOps.
[06:58] Priya Mehta: We'll include a token distribution spreadsheet and cost model.
[07:02] Leah Kim: A small ask — do you support SAML SSO for admin console and RBAC groups?
[07:09] Jordan Park: Yes, SAML/SSO and SCIM for provisioning are supported in the enterprise console. We'll include the SAML metadata sample.
[07:17] Ibrahim Nadeem: Any export controls or country restrictions we should be aware of? We have customers in restricted jurisdictions.
[07:25] Alex Chen: We follow standard export controls and will list any region-specific limitations. For Private on-prem there's more control.
[07:33] Daniel Ortiz: Can we get a go/no-go list for procurement to check off? Like: SOC2 artifacts, SLA redlines, subprocessors, KMS plan, pricing worksheet?
[07:44] Alex Chen: Yes — action checklist: 1) SLA redline 2) DPA updates + subprocessors 3) SOC2 summary and artifacts 4) pricing worksheet and runbook 5) pilot criteria. We'll send as a checklist in the follow-up email.
[07:55] Maya Torres: For pilot success criteria we want throughput at X tokens/sec, P99 latency under 500ms for 512 tokens, no data leakage incidents, and KMS integration validated.
[08:06] Priya Mehta: We'll translate that into measurable tests.
[08:12] Leah Kim: On indemnity, one last note — our legal team will propose a mutual indemnity with a carveout for breaches due to customer misuse. Expect redlines.
[08:21] Alex Chen: Noted. We'll review and respond.
[08:27] Daniel Ortiz: Ok let's recap next steps.
[08:30] Alex Chen: Recap: Redwood sends SLA redlines and pricing worksheet by 2026-04-16; perf test plan and runbook by 2026-04-18; SOC2 summary PDF and subprocessors list in same thread; Atlas provides KMS/IAM requirements and pilot success criteria by 2026-04-20. We'll schedule the baseline benchmark the week of 2026-04-27.
[08:55] Maya Torres: Sounds good. Thanks everyone.
[08:58] Jordan Park: Thanks - I'll circulate the meeting notes and checklist.
[09:02] Alex Chen: Great. Meeting adjourned.

Notes on transcript character and fidelity: Some brand names and product names are slightly off in the audio engine (e.g., "Redwood Dedicated pool" transcribed as "Redwood dedicate pul" at times).
